name: 1995.102  Anglo-Scandinavian antler comb
description:
The Anglo-Scandinavian antler comb was excavated at Jarrow, England, in 1976, within a late-Saxon context, and forms part of the Jarrow Hall collection. Carved from deer antler, the comb exhibits fine craftsmanship characteristic of Anglo-Scandinavian personal grooming tools commonly found in 9th–11th-century contexts across northern England.

Combs of this type were typically constructed from flat antler plates riveted together, featuring closely spaced fine teeth for delousing and grooming. The Jarrow example displays decorative incisions along the spine, consistent with Scandinavian-influenced styles seen in York and Lincoln.

(References: Cramp, 2006; Ashby, 2009; Ambrosiani, 1981.)

name: Cordylus angolensis - MNCN50648
description:
**Description**: This 3D model features the Angolan girdled lizard, a reptile endemic to the rocky highlands of Angola. As the neotype for the species, this specimen serves as the definitive global reference for the species' identity. The visualization offers a detailed look at its heavily armored morphology, characteristic of a genus known for its unique ovoviviparous reproduction. By retaining and hatching eggs internally, this lizard ensures its offspring are born fully developed and protected, a key survival strategy in its native high-altitude habitats.

**Specimen**: *Cordylus angolensis* (Bocage, 1895).

**Inventory number**: MNCN-50648

**Collection**: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, Herpetology. Curator: Marta Calvo (mcalvo@mncn.csic.es).

**More about**:

Find more about the MNCN [here](http:mncn.csic.es/en).

name: Brain of Silver Arowana
description:
The silver arowana Osteoglossum bicirrhosum (Cuvier 1829) is a large, benthopelagic freshwater fish belonging to the order Osteoglossiformes (commonly known as bony tongues). It is native to South America, with a distribution that includes the Amazon River basin, as well as the Rupununi and Oyapock Rivers.

This species is omnivorous, with a strong tendency to feed on fish and other prey at the water surface. Its superior mouth position allows it to capture prey by striking from below—a behavior that includes leaping out of the water to catch insects or even small birds.

The 3D model presented here represents the encephalon (brain) of the silver arowana. Major brain regions are clearly identifiable, including the olfactory bulbs, telencephalon, optic tectum, cerebellum, and medulla oblongata. It is part of a project that aims to compare the structure of the brains of different vertebrate groups and, therefore, facilitate the study of their neuroanatomy.

description:
The reciprocal apparatus is part of the passive stay-apparatus in equines. 
It consists of the **M. fibularis tertius (Tendo femorotarseus)** and the **M. flexor digitorum superficialis (Tendo plantaris)**. 

These nearly tendinous muscles link the actions of the stifle and the hock joints so that they move in unision when it comes to flexion and extension.
Moreover, if the stifle joint is locked the hock joint is also automatically incapable of movement.

3D scanning of bones performed with the structured light scanners “Artec Leo” and “Artec Space Spider”.
Modeling of muscles and animation done in Blender.
